key_insight: ReContext improves long-context reasoning by recursively replaying relevant evidence so the model can better use information that is already in the prompt. Instead of just giving an LLM a longer window, it helps the model repeatedly revisit the most useful context.
problem_solved: LLMs often fail to exploit relevant details in long inputs, even when those details are within the context window. This paper addresses the gap between having access to long context and actually reasoning over it effectively.
method: Uses Recursive Evidence Replay: a training-free inference strategy that re-injects key evidence into the reasoning process.
Selects and replays relevant context iteratively to strengthen the model's attention to important details.
Acts as an LLM harness for long-context tasks, aiming to improve reasoning without modifying model weights.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ReContext offers a practical way to boost long-context performance without retraining or changing the base model. It is especially useful for applications like document QA, legal analysis, research assistants, and multi-step reasoning over lengthy inputs.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing long input -> evidence selection -> recursive replay -> improved answer
Before/after comparison of vanilla LLM vs ReContext on the same long-context task

Icon set representing long documents, repeated loops, and improved reasoning
paper_title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
paper_authors: Yanjun Zhao, Ruizhong Qiu, Tianxin Wei, Yuanchen Bei, Zhining Liu
